top_sql.statement: SELECT o.order_id, o.created_at, o.status, oi.product_id, oi.quantity, oi.unit_price FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.customer_id = $1 ORDER BY o.created_at DESC LIMIT 100
INSERT INTO payment_events (event_id, tenant_id, customer_id, amount, status, created_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, NOW())
SELECT tenant_id, plan, billing_status FROM tenants WHERE tenant_id = $1

notes: Top SQL #1 (orders+order_items JOIN by customer_id) dominates db_load at 6.3 AAS (~77% of total). Per-call duration is normal (~22 ms, CPU-bound, no slow plan). Call rate climbed from a baseline of ~10/sec to 76/sec — a ~7-8x increase concentrated in a single tenant's workload, not a spread-across-tenants surge.
Top SQL #2 (payment_events INSERT) is the normal write path; call rate is normal across all tenants.
Top SQL #3 (tenants lookup) is the typical session-bootstrap query; rates stayed in baseline range.
Top SQL #4 (materialized view refresh) is a scheduled background task; unchanged.

Top users decisively attribute the load to one tenant: acme_app_user at 6.4 AAS (~78% of total) while globex_app_user and initech_app_user remain at baseline (~0.4-0.5 AAS each). This is a tenant-attribution scenario, not a system-wide regression.

Top hosts confirm tenant attribution: only two 10.0.1.x IPs appear (10.0.1.11 and 10.0.1.12 — acme-corp's two API instances), and together they account for ~78% of total db_load. The 10.0.2.x and 10.0.3.x IPs belong to globex and initech respectively and each contribute under 0.3 AAS. The single 10.0.4.x IP is the shared background worker.
